state.objective: Determine the proper treatment of 70 legacy affiliate/interunit account families under a centralized HO-unit operating model. Do not assume accounts are valid merely because they exist.
confirmed_operating_facts: HO controls all finance and bank access.
Units handle limited physical operations and cannot transact directly with other units.
Allowed operational relationship is HO-unit only; no unit-to-unit route.
Unit/site is already stored as site_id and removed from the natural account suffix.
No general counter_site_id or related_site_id will be added to journal lines.
Operational transfers can carry origin_site_id and destination_site_id on shipment/transfer documents.
It is still unknown whether all named sites are branches of one legal entity or whether any are separate legal entities/affiliates.
No balances, posting history, settlement, elimination process or legal-entity master has been supplied.

receivable_42: Piutang Affiliasi Pembiayaan: 14 named HO/site counterpart families
Piutang Affiliasi Atas Barang: 14 named HO/site counterpart families
Piutang Affiliasi Lain-lain: 14 named HO/site counterpart families
payable_28: Hutang Affiliasi Pembiayaan: 14 named HO/site counterpart families

actual_legacy_pattern.historical_matrix: Each family was also repeated through the old E1 site suffix, implying a possible owning-site by named-counterparty matrix. This structure permits unit-to-unit combinations even though the confirmed process disallows them.

same_entity_receivable.instructions: If HO and every unit are branches/sites of the same legal entity, are balances between those sites external receivables and payables of that legal entity?

criteria.no: They are internal branch/clearing balances, not third-party receivables/payables in entity-level financial statements.
criteria.yes: Every site relationship is an external receivable/payable.
criteria.always_affiliate: The word Affiliasi proves separate legal entities.

same_entity_target.instructions: If all sites are one legal entity and books are centralized, what is the safest target for the 70 families?

criteria.audit_reclass_close: Audit balances; reclassify to the underlying cash/inventory/expense/clearing nature, retain only necessary temporary clearing controls, and block obsolete route accounts.
criteria.keep_70: Keep all affiliate receivable/payable GLs by site.
criteria.merge_one_ar: Merge all 70 into one external receivable account.

branch_clearing.instructions: For one legal entity, is a permanent due-to/from account required for every HO-unit route?

criteria.no: Only use limited clearing accounts if a real timing/control need exists; reconcile and clear them through the underlying workflow.
criteria.yes: Create permanent receivable and payable GLs for each site route.
criteria.matrix: Maintain the full all-to-all site matrix.

separate_entity_target.instructions: If some sites are separate legal entities, should counterparty names remain encoded in natural GL accounts?

criteria.dimension: Use counterparty_legal_entity_id/intercompany partner; retain natural accounts by receivable/payable and transaction nature needed for reporting/elimination.
criteria.gl_names: Keep one natural GL per named counterparty site.
criteria.site_only: Use operational site_id as a substitute for legal entity.

five_natures.instructions: Under a separate-legal-entity scenario, can the 70 location-specific families provisionally reduce to the five existing natures: receivable-financing, receivable-goods, receivable-other, payable-financing and payable-goods, with counterparty legal entity detail?

criteria.conditional: Yes, if classification, maturity, currency, settlement, eliminations and reporting align.
criteria.retain_70: Counterparty identity must stay in GL.
criteria.one: Combine all receivables and payables into one net account.

ar_ap_netting.instructions: Can receivable and payable balances be netted into one natural account merely because the counterparty is related?

criteria.no: Keep asset and liability presentation unless enforceable set-off criteria and settlement intent are demonstrated.
criteria.site: Same site name permits automatic netting.

ho_unit_route.instructions: Where should the HO-unit-only route restriction be enforced?

criteria.workflow: In transfer/funding documents and permissions, with allowed origin/destination rules.
criteria.coa: By creating a GL for each allowed pair.

counter_site_again.instructions: Does resolving the 70 legacy families require reversing the decision and adding a general counter_site_id to journals?

criteria.no: Use legal-entity partner only when legally relevant and document-level route fields for operations.
criteria.gl: Encode counter-site into natural GL instead.

inactive_zero_accounts.instructions: If unit-to-unit route accounts have zero balances and no valid transactions, should they be migrated as active posting accounts?

criteria.no: Preserve legacy mapping/history but deactivate or omit them from active posting COA.
criteria.yes: Migrate all as active because they existed historically.
criteria.merge: Post their zero balances into miscellaneous expense.

nonzero_invalid_routes.instructions: If disallowed unit-to-unit accounts contain balances, can they simply be deleted?

criteria.no: Trace transactions, counterpart balances, ownership and settlement; reclassify/reconcile with an auditable migration entry.
criteria.yes: Delete balances because the future workflow disallows them.

minimum_evidence.instructions: What evidence is required to close this domain?

criteria.full: Legal-entity/site master, trial balances by account/site, transaction samples, counterpart matching, settlement process, consolidation/elimination policy and aging.

safe_now.instructions: What may be approved before that evidence arrives?

criteria.architecture: Approve HO-unit route workflow, no general counter_site, conditional legal-entity partner model, and an audit/deactivation plan; do not approve balance mappings yet.
criteria.delete70: Delete all 70 accounts and balances immediately.
